item.title: Canada boss Marsch calls for severe punishment for Man City
item.description: Canada coach Jesse Marsch has called for Manchester City to be punished severely over breaches of Premier League financial rules, saying his experience managing against the club left him convinced there were inconsistencies in the way it operated.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada coach Jesse Marsch has called for Manchester City to be punished severely over breaches of Premier League financial rules, saying his experience managing against the club left him convinced there were inconsistencies in the way it operated. City were found guilty of [USN:L6N45L10S TEXT:"serious breaches"] of Premier League financial rules over nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, with the league alleging the club used "sham" commercial contracts to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19 billion). The club has denied wrongdoing, saying the verdict contained material errors of law, principle and fact, and [USN:L1N45O0BQ TEXT:"filed an appeal"] on Thursday against the independent commission ruling. Marsch, who managed Leeds United from 2022 to 2023, said the disparity between the clubs had been apparent to him during his time in England. "I think Man City should be punished severely. I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew," Marsch told the Guardian in an interview published on Sunday. Marsch also pointed to the 2022 summer transfer window, when Leeds sold Raphinha to Barcelona and Kalvin Phillips to City, while both clubs reported making money. "That summer (2022), us and Man City were the only teams that said we made money. For us, we did make money, because we sold Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips. We had a lot left over from what we bought," he said. "At the time, we weren't in a position financially to not save. Our ownership didn't have deep pockets. Whereas when Man City says this, I was literally like, 'Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?'" The American coach was also sceptical about City's signing of Erling Haaland from Borussia Dortmund that summer. "When they said they got Erling Haaland for £52m, it's like: 'Yeah, OK, sure!' So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, 'This is football'," Marsch said. Reuters has contacted Manchester City for comment on Marsch's remarks. City's appeal will be heard privately by an independent three-member board. Potential sanctions include fines, points deductions and other sporting penalties, with relegation or the removal of titles also discussed as possible outcomes. It remains unclear whether any sanctions would be imposed before the appeal is decided. ($1 = 0.7554 pounds)

item.title: A roadmap for Andy Burnham to reverse Brexit
item.description: Britain’s prime minister says the country could rejoin the European Union. To do so, he will first have to decide if he wants to take that step, then win an election, and then persuade the 27-country bloc to readmit its former member. Here is how he could go about it.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Dixon
item.content:encoded: Andy Burnham [USN:L8N45L233 TEXT:"said"] last week that the United Kingdom could “go all the way” and rejoin the European Union. How could Britain’s new prime minister complete such a journey given the trauma Britain has suffered following the 2016 Brexit referendum and the trouble it inflicted on its European partners in the process? Burnham will have to start by deciding that he definitely wants to rejoin the EU. He will then have to win a general election based on that premise and then persuade the 27-country bloc to readmit its former member. Here is a roadmap. Burnham said in his speech to his Labour Party’s conference that “Brexit has done more harm than good”. Britain’s economic output is 6-8% lower than it would have been if it had stayed in the EU, according to a recent paper published by the National Bureau of Economic Research. Brexit has also damaged both the UK’s and the EU’s power, weakening the continent at a time of geopolitical turmoil. The prime minister laid out a series of options, only one of which was to rejoin the EU. The alternatives are to join Europe’s customs union or single market, negotiate a bespoke deal with the bloc like the one Canada is discussing, or leave things as they are. There are good reasons for going the whole way. Becoming a member of the EU’s customs union would simplify trade in goods across the English Channel. But it would not boost trade in services, which accounts for about 80% of UK output. It would also require Britain to align its trade policy with the EU’s but not have any vote on it. Joining the single market would smooth trade in services as well as goods. However, Britain would have to accept free movement of people across the EU and follow all the bloc’s economic regulations, again without a say in how they are formed. Canada and the EU are discussing joining forces to help them both resist intimidation by China, the United States and Russia. The [USN:L6N45A0WZ TEXT:"idea"] is to boost resilience in everything from energy and rare earths to technology and defence equipment. While the UK also needs to stand up to bullies, it is more closely entwined with the EU than Canada. So although a “resilience pact” could be a good step to rejoining, full membership with a seat at the decision-making table remains the best destination. CONVINCING VOTERS Burnham says a decision on rejoining the EU would have to wait until after a general election, which must be held no later than 2029. His Labour Party is favourite to win the most seats, probably without an overall majority, according to Oddschecker. But it is vying with Reform UK, the anti-EU party led by Nigel Farage, for first place. One reason for going all the way is that this is more popular than joining either the single market or the customs union, according to polling by YouGov for Best for Britain, the pro-EU group. Their research also shows that Labour will perform better at the next election if it backs full EU membership. Burnham would still have to win the election, though. Key to this would be to convince voters that rejoining the EU would help address their main concerns: migration, the economy, security, and health. This is where the prime minister’s charisma should be an asset. If Labour won a general election, perhaps forming a coalition with the pro-European Liberal Democrats, that would not be the end of the story. Burnham says there might also be a referendum on reversing Brexit. One way to make it easier to win such a plebiscite would be to offer voters a simple question about the principle of rejoining the EU, while leaving the details to parliament. This would be a mirror image of the Brexit referendum, which consulted voters before the government had negotiated an exit deal. Such a vote could take place immediately after an election. CONVINCING THE EU Even then, however, Britain could not re-enter the bloc by expressing its desire to do so. It would have to persuade the EU’s 27 existing members to let it back into the club. The UK would not get the same terms it enjoyed before, when it received a £4.5 billion rebate on its annual membership fee. It might also have to sign up to eventually join the euro, though this would not necessarily be a dealbreaker. EU members such as Poland and Sweden still have their currencies. Britain has much to contribute to the EU. Its capable military and its $4.3 trillion economy, Europe’s second largest after Germany’s, are key assets. A trickier challenge will be persuading the EU that Britain is coming back for good. Even if Burnham charms the bloc’s leaders, starting with a summit planned for November, they will worry that a future anti-EU government in Westminster will pull the UK out for a second time. While the prime minister cannot give a cast-iron guarantee that this will not happen, he can mitigate the risk. His plan to [USN:S8N44301D TEXT:"change"] Britain's voting system if he wins the next election would, if successful, make it impossible for an anti-EU party to obtain a parliamentary majority with as little as 30% of the vote, as is theoretically the case today. Under a more proportional voting system, a future anti-EU government would need the support of nearer half the electorate to push through its agenda. What is more, if Burnham called a referendum to take Britain back into the EU, he could set the threshold of consent at, say, 55% or 60%. This would help establish the precedent that a similar super majority would be needed for any subsequent attempt to take the UK out. The EU is weak and divided. Whether it rises to the [USN:L6N3XB0W3 TEXT:"challenges"] presented by Russia, China and the United States and tackles its own economic woes will help determine whether the UK wants to rejoin. If far-right parties take power in France and Germany, the EU will be a less attractive club. By contrast, if the bloc boosts its defences, helps Ukraine stave off Russia’s invasion and enacts long-promised reforms to boost its productivity, Burnham – and many Britons – will be clamouring to rejoin. item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) não atirou no chão uma bandeira do Brasil após votar neste domingo, como alegam posts nas redes sociais que reproduzem um vídeo omitindo o momento em que Lula entrega o item ao seu fotógrafo, Ricardo Stuckert . Estes são os principais detalhes: “Revoltante! Lula amassa bandeira do Brasil e joga no chão”, dizem publicações no Facebook, no Instagram e no Threads com as imagens. O presidente votou em São Bernardo do Campo (SP) e posou para fotos ao lado do vice-presidente e candidato à reeleição, Geraldo Alckmin (PSB), segurando a bandeira nacional. Logo em seguida, Lula caminha para deixar o local de votação e entrega rapidamente a bandeira a Stuckert, mas o enquadramento do vídeo usado nos posts checados não permite ver a passagem do objeto para o fotógrafo. O momento em que Lula entregou a bandeira a Stuckert apareceu na transmissão ao vivo da GloboNews . Veredicto: Falso. Lula entregou ao seu fotógrafo a bandeira do Brasil após votar, e não a jogou no chão. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: Improving special teams high on Bruins' agenda as Senators visit
item.description: Another first is on tap for the Boston Bruins.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Another first is on tap for the Boston Bruins. After splitting a back-to-back road trip, Boston opens a three-game homestand with its first Atlantic Division test of the season against the Ottawa Senators on Monday night. The Bruins could not pull off a sweep of two teams playing their home openers, taking a 4-1 loss to the Minnesota Wild on Saturday after beating the Winnipeg Jets 4-3 on JJ Peterka's game-winner in overtime a night earlier. "Special teams were probably the difference, both ways. But I really liked our 5-on-5 game," Boston coach Marco Sturm said in Minnesota. "We didn't really give them much. Our first period was outstanding. A lot of good things happened (on Saturday). ... Guys battled hard. They really did." Both of Boston's specialty units have struggled, with the power play yet to score in six chances and the penalty kill going 4-for-7. On Saturday, Tanner Jeannot gave the Bruins a 1-0 lead in just 1:53, but Minnesota took control with a pair of power-play goals in the second period. Fellow fourth-liner Mark Kastelic set up Jeannot's goal with a touch feed through his legs, giving him a team-high three points (one goal, two assists). "He's been playing unreal. I told him before the game, 'Just keep doing what you're doing,'" Jeannot said. "He's the heartbeat of this team. He's doing everything -- he's putting his body on the line, he's getting points right now. It's been a lot of fun playing with him." Peterka scored in Boston's first two games. He recorded his third straight 25-goal season last year with the Utah Mammoth, who play in Boston on Thursday. The Bruins figure to turn back to Jeremy Swayman in goal after reigning AHL Most Valuable Player Michael DiPietro made his Boston debut with a 26-save effort. It was the 27-year-old's first NHL start since 2022, when he was a member of the Vancouver Canucks. "You definitely learn from your mistakes. Like I said, obviously not the outcome that I wanted, and I own that," DiPietro said. "I just have to be better and continue to work and try my best." Ottawa's wait for its season opener -- the longest of any NHL team -- was worth it after a 3-2 win over the host Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday. However, top defenseman Jake Sanderson played only 4:29 before exiting with a nagging lower-body injury, and there was no update on his status following the game. The Senators were already starting the season without defenseman Artem Zub (knee). "We'll know more in the next few days, but Sandy was smart enough to pull himself early enough that he didn't reaggravate it too badly," Ottawa coach Travis Green said. "He just felt that it was coming and took himself out." Sanderson, who left a preseason game a week earlier with a different injury, smashed his stick in frustration upon returning to the bench. "He's going to put everything he can into it and he'll be back in no time," new Senators captain Thomas Chabot said of Sanderson. Following Sanderson's exit, the Senators had to rally from a 2-1 deficit, outshooting their archrivals 16-5 in the final frame and getting the game-winning goal from Stephen Halliday with 10:14 remaining. Chabot had a goal and an assist while playing 27:06, Michael Amadio also scored and Claude Giroux dished out a pair of helpers. Former Bruin Linus Ullmark, who went on a 14-4-3 run late last season, made 27 saves to lift Ottawa to its third straight season-opening win under Green. "I thought the third period was our best," Chabot said. "We played exactly the way that we wanted to play. I'm just glad we got it done." --Field Level Media

item.title: Britain set to levy tariffs on Chinese electric cars, The Times reports
item.description: Britain is considering imposing tariffs on Chinese electric vehicle imports amid concerns that Beijing is flooding the market with state-subsidised cars, the Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain is considering imposing tariffs on Chinese electric vehicle imports amid concerns that Beijing is flooding the market with state-subsidised cars, the Times newspaper reported on Sunday. Business minister Jonathan Reynolds is drawing up a package of potential tariffs on Chinese vehicle imports, the report said, citing concerns that Chinese manufacturers are "dumping" subsidised vehicles into Britain. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Asked to comment, a spokesperson from the British government told Reuters no tariffs have been imposed on Chinese EVs. "We continue to engage closely with industry so that our approach reflects the sector’s and UK’s national interests," the spokesperson said in an email. British ministers are ready to match the European Union's 45% levy on Chinese electric cars, the Times said, to avoid the pain of "Made in Europe" proposals, which could impact UK companies selling into the EU. The EU's "[USN:L8N42K09E TEXT:"Made in Europe"]" policy is aimed at reducing reliance on Chinese components by prioritising European-made goods, raising concerns among British automakers that supply parts into European manufacturing chains and sell vehicles across the bloc. Burnham [USN:L8N45E0EA TEXT:"said"] last month he would make the case that Britain should be treated as a "trusted partner" under the proposed EU rules, warning that excluding the UK could damage its car industry. The Financial Times reported in September [USN:FWN45G1EO TEXT:"that Brussels had urged"] British Prime Minister Andy Burnham to align more closely with EU trade policy and raise tariffs on Chinese cars if Britain wants to avoid the "made in Europe" barriers. According to the Times, citing senior government sources, ministers believe any decision on tariffs should be based on Britain's national interest rather than automatically following the EU's lead.

item.title: FIA to investigate software bug after Bahrain GP in Malaysia
item.description: Formula One's governing body has promised a full investigation into a software bug that caused chaos and forced the start of Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to be aborted with drivers feeling like they were in battery-powered cars made of Lego.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Formula One's governing body has promised a full investigation into a software bug that caused chaos and forced the start of Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to be aborted with drivers feeling like they were in battery-powered cars made of Lego. Ferrari's seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's four-time champion and[USN:L1N45Q023 TEXT:" eventual race winner Max Verstappen "]were among several affected by the glitch on a formation lap after torrential rain and [USN:L1N45Q01D TEXT:"a long delay "]at Malaysia's steamy Sepang circuit. Verstappen compared the experience to a[USN:L6N43703Y TEXT:" 'Lego race"]' held at Silverstone before the British Grand Prix while Hamilton, the sport's most successful driver of all time, had to stop his car on track and re-start it in what he said was a career first. The episode was the latest in a difficult first season for the new era of cars and engines, with drivers at the pinnacle of motorsport unhappy since the opening race with the power units' increased electrical component and the need for energy management. The governing FIA said afterwards that "an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars." "As a result, the FIA technical department removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release distributed to all competitors during the race delay caused by heavy rain, enabling teams to make the necessary changes to the power unit before the start of the race. “This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or during the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue." The FIA's single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis told reporters the lack of pre-season testing in wet conditions had played a part in the chaos. "Some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely," he said. “That bug prevented the power from being redeployed, and for the cars to start again. "I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time, and not have such a situation." Sepang was the first race weekend of the season with wet conditions, although the track dried during the race. "Sometimes things fall through the net and people learn, and you do a better job next time,” said Tombazis.

item.title: US removes B-1 bombers from UK base amid security concerns
item.description: The United States removed its B-1 bombers from a UK air base one week after several men were arrested there on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a Pentagon official said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Svea Herbst-Bayliss
item.content:encoded: The United States removed its B-1 bombers from a UK air base one week after several men were arrested there on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a Pentagon official said on Sunday. A dozen B-1 bombers were stationed at RAF Fairford air base, located northwest of London. The planes had been used for US strikes on Iran. "While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time, we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States," a Pentagon spokesman wrote in an email. Britain has "strong indications" that [USN:L1N45M0MW TEXT:"Iran was involved"] in a [USN:L1N45O076 TEXT:"suspected plot"] targeting the base, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday. Iran said accusations linking Tehran to the alleged plan were baseless and summoned the British ambassador in Tehran over the issue. The Wall Street Journal first reported that the aircraft were removed from the base amid security concerns over suspected terror plots against the facility. The British government had allowed the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. US President [USN:L8N45K0CX TEXT:"Donald Trump said those involved in the plot"] had planned "big damage" while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also pointed to the "hands of a foreign actor."

item.title: Portugal secure place in Nations League quarter-finals
item.description: Title holders Portugal maintained their 100% record in the Nations League with a 2-1 home win over Norway on Sunday to seal a place in the March quarter-finals and shift the focus further away from Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt exit from the squad last week.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: Title holders Portugal maintained their 100% record in the Nations League with a 2-1 home win over Norway on Sunday to seal a place in the March quarter-finals and shift the focus further away from Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt exit from the squad last week. Goncalo Ramos netted 11 minutes from time to ensure Portugal secured a top-two finish in Group A4 as they moved six points ahead of second-placed Denmark, who won 1-0 at Wales. The Netherlands took over at the top of Group A2, after beating Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven, but only on goal difference from Greece, who held on grimly for a goalless draw at home to Germany in Thessaloniki. Portugal were still under a cloud from Ronaldo’s dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, although they were triumphant without him in Denmark last Thursday after he walked out on the squad, and continued their winning ways in Porto on Sunday. Norway took the lead in the 36th minute from centre-back Kristoffer Ajer, who hit a dipping half-volley from the edge of the box. But if that effort was sumptuous, Joao Cancelo’s thrashing effort to equalise two minutes later was even more awe-inspiring. Ramos’ winner came off his calf after Joao Felix had headed across goal for him to score. “You need a lot of technical quality to beat Norway," said the Portugal coach. "We won without putting in a performance like the one against Denmark, but the important thing was the victory and qualification. I had a lot of belief in this team, but perhaps I didn’t expect us to have four wins from our first four games,” Jorge Jesus added. RED CARD SOURS PORTUGAL'S WIN Portugal’s win was soured by a red card for Francisco Conceicao four minutes from time. He gave the referee a cynical thumbs up after receiving a yellow card and was immediately handed his marching orders. Wales goalkeeper Danny Ward made several key saves to keep Denmark at bay in Cardiff, but then conceded a penalty with a foul on Gustav Isaksen, allowing Rasmus Hojlund to tuck away a 75th-minute penalty to win their tie. The Netherlands, with captain Virgil van Dijk celebrating a 100th cap, went ahead against Serbia when Teun Koopmeiners’s 31st-minute freekick evaded all in the penalty area and crept into the corner. But the visitors were level within four minutes as Aleksa Terzic crossed for teenager Mihajlo Cvetkovic to rise over Koopmeiners and head in his first international goal. ZIRKZEE GRABS DUTCH WINNER It took until the 72nd minute to go back ahead when Denzel Dumfries’ low cross was turned back across the goal by Tijjani Reijnders, sliding in at the far post, and tapped in by Joshua Zirkzee, who received a late call-up to the Dutch squad last week. Germany dominated away against Greece, but Jurgen Klopp’s inexperienced side could not find the net, and they have won only one of their first four games under the new coach. Austria needed a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Kosovo but still have a three-point lead at the top of Group B3 after the Republic of Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 behind closed doors in the Serbian town of Backa Topola. In Group D2, Abdulakh Khaybulayev’s first-half goal was enough to send Azerbaijan top of the standings with a 1-0 win over previously unbeaten Lithuania, while veteran Teddy Teuma came on as a second-half substitute to hand Malta a 1-0 home win over Andorra in Group D1.

item.title: Posts inventam resultados de votações no exterior ainda em andamento
item.description: Posts nas redes sociais sobre as eleições deste domingo inventam resultados de votações no exterior ainda em andamento, como nos Estados Unidos e no Canadá, e os misturam com supostos números impressos nos boletins de urna de países onde o pleito já se encerrou.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Posts nas redes sociais sobre as eleições deste domingo inventam resultados de votações no exterior ainda em andamento, como nos Estados Unidos e no Canadá, e os misturam com supostos números impressos nos boletins de urna de países onde o pleito já se encerrou. O conteúdo tem o título “votação no exterior” e diz mostrar os resultados atualizados “conforme boletins divulgados” pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), reproduzindo uma lista de 42 países e as supostas votações dos candidatos Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em cada um. A montagem, que circula no Facebook e no Instagram, afirma que Lula obteve 23.992 votos no exterior, enquanto Flávio somou 71.601. Há 918.876 eleitores aptos a votar em 186 cidades no exterior, segundo o TSE, exclusivamente para o cargo de presidente. Em todos os países, a votação ocorre das 8h às 17h, de acordo com o fuso horário local . Por isso, a votação teve início às 16h deste sábado em Wellington, capital da Nova Zelândia, e terminará às 21h deste domingo em San Francisco e Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos, e em Vancouver, no Canadá, segundo levantamento do Poder360 . Eleitores de parte dos países mencionados seguiam votando quando os posts começaram a ser compartilhados, na manhã deste domingo, como de Estados Unidos, Canadá, México, Argentina e Chile. Portanto, seria impossível saber o resultado do pleito nesses locais. Nos países da Oceania e da Ásia , a votação já havia encerrado. A apuração oficial só começou a ser divulgada pelo TSE depois das 17h, no horário de Brasília, mas os boletins de urna impressos após o fim da votação permitiram o acesso a alguns desses resultados ao longo deste domingo. Até as 17h45min, com 59,96% das seções no exterior apuradas pelo TSE , Lula tinha 112.644 votos (52,57%) em países estrangeiros, à frente de Flávio, com 81.069 votos (37,83%). VEREDICTO Falso. Os posts divulgam resultados de votações no exterior antes do fechamento das urnas em uma série de países mencionados. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.description: El senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro aventajaba al presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil el domingo, según un recuento preliminar del tribunal electoral del país.

item.content:encoded: El senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro aventajaba al presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil el domingo, según un recuento preliminar del tribunal electoral del país. item.title: Jaguars knock off Bengals, who lose Ja'Marr Chase (concussion)
item.description: Trevor Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown to lead the visiting Jacksonville Jaguars past the Cincinnati Bengals 22-17 on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Trevor Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown to lead the visiting Jacksonville Jaguars past the Cincinnati Bengals 22-17 on Sunday. It was the first time Lawrence defeated Joe Burrow in four career meetings. Bhayshul Tuten ran 17 times for 73 yards while Chris Rodriguez Jr. added a 25-yard touchdown run for the Jaguars (3-1). Burrow was 39-of-54 passing for 428 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. Tee Higgins caught 11 passes for 157 yards while Chase Brown caught 11 passes for 71 yards for the Bengals (2-2). The Jaguars thought they had iced the game on a third-down pass from Lawrence to Parker Washington but replay brought a 39-yard gain back and ruled Washington's heel out of bounds near midfield. The Bengals and Burrow drove to the Jacksonville 21-yard line but on fourth-and-10, a pass for Brown came up short. On second down, Burrow missed an open Mike Gesicki in the end zone for the potential go-ahead score. The Bengals played the second half without star receiver Ja'Marr Chase, who was knocked out of the game with concussion symptoms. He had three catches for 27 yards. With 12 minutes left in the second quarter, Chase took a pass from Joe Burrow at the Jacksonville 30 and had his facemask turned by corner Jarrian Jones. As soon as Jones let go, linebacker Ventrell Miller lowered his helmet and hit Chase in the head, driving the receiver's head into the turf. Chase made it up on his own power, was examined in the tent and went to the locker room for concussion evaluation before being ruled out at halftime. The officiating crew of referee Alex Moore called 24 accepted penalties, including 16 in the first-half penalties in the first half, most in the NFL this season for a half. Each team had touchdown runs wiped out by holding calls. Cincinnati's Samaje Perine had a 14-yard run by a Dylan Fairchild hold while Jacksonville's Tuten had a 44-yard run nullified by Ezra Cleveland. Tuten later had a 3-yard TD run negated by a hold. The Bengals played the game without starting safety Bryan Cook (ankle). Russ Yeast and PJ Jules filled in for Cook. Jacksonville took advantage of a Jourdan Lewis interception of Burrow and a 45-yard return to the Cincinnati 18 to score the game's first touchdown. Lawrence threw a pass over a trio of Cincinnati defenders to a wide-open Brian Thomas Jr. for a 13-3 lead just before halftime. Cincinnati opened the second half with a 12-play, 67-yard drive that ended with Burrow's 15-yard touchdown strike over the middle to Gesicki. With Jacksonville leading 16-10, the Bengals were on the brink of taking the lead. Burrow hit Higgins for 26 yards down to the Jacksonville 10. But on the next play, Burrow threw a pass for Mitch Tinsley that Foyesade Oluokun stepped in front of for an interception. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cowboys stun Texans 34-30 behind CeeDee Lamb, huge second half
item.description: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon. Lamb posted a career-best 17 receptions and totaled 189 yards to help Dallas overcome a 10-point halftime deficit. Jason Witten (18 in 2012) is the only Dallas player to have more receptions in a game. Dak Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and Williams had 62 yards on 19 carries for the Cowboys (2-2). C.J. Stroud was 21-of-31 passing for 347 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans (0-4), who have lost their first four games for the first time since 2020. Houston's Nico Collins caught seven passes for 118 yards and two scores after a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Woody Marks rushed for a score. Stroud guided the Texans on a nine-play, 87-yard drive to take a 30-27 lead with 2:23 left. The pivotal play was on third-and-14 from the Dallas 27-yard line. Stroud threw a short pass to tight end Dalton Schultz at the 25. His lateral to David Montgomery was good for 19 more yards to the Cowboys' 6. Marks scored on the next play. Prescott then drove Dallas 74 yards on 11 plays, eventually connecting with Lamb for the winning points. Dallas trailed by 10 at the break but KaVontae Turpin opened the third quarter with a 48-yard kickoff return to the Texans' 49. Four plays later, Williams scored on an 8-yard run to bring the Cowboys 16-13. Houston answered with its own impressive kickoff return as Jaylin Noel went 53 yards to the Dallas 38. Four plays later, Stroud tossed a 22-yard touchdown pass to Collins to give the Texans a 23-13 advantage with 10:50 left in the quarter. Later in the quarter, Williams scored from the 1 as Dallas pulled within three with 6:49 left. On their next possession, the Cowboys drove 81 yards on 14 plays with Williams scoring on a 2-yard run to give Dallas its first lead at 27-23 with 11:17 left in the game. Stroud threw a touchdown pass to Collins and Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked three field goals as the Texans led 16-6 at halftime. Houston took the opening kickoff and went 85 yards on eight plays. Stroud hit Collins for 45 yards at the outset of the drive and later connected on a 7-yard scoring pass to Collins. Dallas responded with Brandon Aubrey's 39-yard field goal with 5:10 left before Fairbairn was good from 51 yards to give the Texans a 10-3 advantage with 1:49 remaining. Aubrey drilled a 50-yard field goal to bring the Cowboys within 10-6 with 12:30 left in the half. Fairbairn added field goals of 39 and 54. --Field Level Media

item.title: Drake Maye (3 TDs), Patriots stun Bills at home with late score
item.description: Drake Maye completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns, including a late, go-ahead TD pass to Efton Chism III, to lead the New England Patriots to a 29-26 victory over the Buffalo Bills on Sunday in Orchard Park, N.Y.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drake Maye completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns, including a late, go-ahead TD pass to Efton Chism III, to lead the New England Patriots to a 29-26 victory over the Buffalo Bills on Sunday in Orchard Park, N.Y. Chism's leaping, one-handed 23-yard TD catch plus Maye's pass to Rhamondre Stevenson for the two-point conversion gave the Patriots a 29-26 lead with 1:50 to play. Craig Woodson intercepted a Josh Allen pass at the New England 19-yard line on the ensuing possession, and the Patriots (2-2) were able to run out the clock and hand Buffalo (3-1) its first loss in its new stadium. Allen was 23-of-33 passing for 253 yards and one touchdown. Buffalo's Keon Coleman caught six passes for 116 yards and a TD. James Cook rushed for 75 yards and a score. The Patriots struck first when Maye connected with Romeo Doubs (six receptions, 58 yards, two TDs) for a 14-yard touchdown pass with 7:01 left in the first quarter. The score capped a 12-play, 97-yard drive. Buffalo tied the game on Cook's 8-yard TD run plus Tyler Bass' extra point 45 seconds into the second quarter. New England regained the lead on Stevenson's 1-yard run with 5:38 left before halftime, but Buffalo responded when Allen scored from 2 yards away with one minute left. The TD gave Allen the most touchdowns from scrimmage (88) in franchise history, breaking a tie with Andre Reed and Thurman Thomas. It remained 14-14 until Bass made a 27-yard field goal with two seconds left in the half. The field goal was set up by Dee Alford's interception that he returned to the New England 9-yard line with nine seconds remaining. The interception came after Doubs lost control of the ball as he fell to the ground following a catch. The Patriots were up 21-17 after Doubs caught a 2-yard TD pass with 8:15 left in the third, but Buffalo made it 21-20 on Bass' 38-yard field goal with 11:07 to play in the game. The Bills regained their lead at 26-21 on Allen's 34-yard TD pass to Coleman with 4:27 left. The ensuing two-point conversion attempt failed. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jameis Winston, Giants outlast Cardinals to move to 3-1
item.description: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdown passes and the New York Giants outlasted the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdown passes and the New York Giants outlasted the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J. Winston overcame two interceptions and four sacks to complete 18 of 29 passes for 250 yards. He found tight end Theo Johnson on an 11-yard connection late in the third quarter for the go-ahead score. In a back-and-forth game with three lead changes and six turnovers, the Giants (3-1) had to climb out of a 14-3 first-quarter hole. New York turned things around with Winston's touchdown passes to Malachi Fields and Malik Nabers in the final 4:30 of the first half, which followed the second of three Dominic Zvada field goals. The Giants' halftime lead was cut to 19-17 when the Cardinals' Chad Ryland booted a 60-yard field goal as time expired. The Cardinals reclaimed the lead midway through the third quarter when Jacoby Brissett found a wide-open Elijah Higgins over the middle for a 2-yard touchdown pass to make it 24-19. But they couldn't come up with any more points as they ventured into Giants territory just once in their final four possessions. Arizona (1-3) lost its third straight game after a season-opening road win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett completed 21 of 35 passes for 166 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions, including a pick-6 on the game's final play. Giants running back Cam Skattebo ran for a key first down with just over three minutes left to allow New York to take more time off the clock, but the Giants settled for a 52-yard field goal by Zvada with 2:11 to play. The Cardinals had one more chance. Deonte Banks was whistled for an 18-yard pass interference call on a pass intended for Marvin Harrison Jr., which moved the Cardinals down to the Giants' 4-yard line with 22 seconds to play. After Brissett threw three straight incomplete passes, Banks redeemed himself on fourth down by intercepting Brissett and returning it 98 yards for a touchdown as the clock ran out. The Cardinals lost starting offensive tackle Paris Johnson Jr. to injury on the final drive. Earlier in the game, right guard Isaiah Adams and safety Andrew Wingard (knee) were carted off. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lamar Jackson exits, Ravens hold on to beat Titans
item.description: Lamar Jackson threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-20 passing but exited early in the Ravens' 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday in Baltimore.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-20 passing but exited early in the Ravens' 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday in Baltimore. The Ravens (3-1) snapped a four-game losing streak in their home stadium but needed their defense to hang on after the Titans (0-4) held them scoreless in the second half without Jackson, who did not play after halftime. Jackson was sacked on Baltimore's final play of the second quarter by Jermaine Johnson II, who landed on Jackson's left ankle. Jackson was later seen on the sideline with his ankle wrapped. Tyler Huntley played the rest of the game and completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards and ran for 16 yards on four attempts. The Ravens were held scoreless after taking a 24-7 lead to the half. Cam Ward's 3-yard touchdown pass to Wan'Dale Robinson and two-point conversion pass to Gunnar Helm pulled the Titans within six with 1:12 left. But Malaki Starks recovered Tennessee's ensuing onside kick with 1:10 left and Baltimore ran out the clock. The Titans, who lost their first four games for the second consecutive season, were held to just a 33-yard field goal by Joey Slye in the second half until that late score. Tennessee committed two costly first-half turnovers -- an interception by Ward and a fumble after a catch by Carnell Tate -- which led to 10 points for the Ravens. Ward completed 20 of 31 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown and was intercepted on the Titans' first drive by Trenton Simpson. Tate caught nine passes for 145 yards. Baltimore also stopped Tennessee on fourth down at the Ravens' 2 with 8:16 left in the second quarter. Nnamdi Madubuike stopped Tony Pollard short of a touchdown that would have tied the game at 14. The Ravens responded with an eight-play, 98-yard drive that ended with Jackson finding Mark Andrews open in the end zone for a 3-yard touchdown to put Baltimore ahead 21-7. Derrick Henry beat his former team for the first time and finished with 73 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries. Zay Flowers caught eight passes for 118 yards and a touchdown. Baltimore kicker Tyler Loop continued his hot streak by making a 64-yard field goal as time expired in the first half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jordan Love, Packers' defense keep Bucs winless
item.description: Jordan Love threw two touchdown passes and the Green Bay Packers' defense picked off a pair of passes en route to a 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday in Tampa.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jordan Love threw two touchdown passes and the Green Bay Packers' defense picked off a pair of passes en route to a 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday in Tampa. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards and Tucker Kraft had six catches for 42 yards and a score for the Packers (2-2), who moved to 2-0 on the road. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, making his first start, completed 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions for Tampa Bay (0-4), which remained the NFC's last winless team. Daniels also rushed for 55 yards playing in place of the injured Baker Mayfield. Leading 10-7 at halftime, Green Bay opened the second half with an eight-play scoring drive that Love capped with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Kraft. Daniels answered with the first touchdown pass of his career as he hit Kenneth Gainwell for a 10-yard score to cut the Buccaneers' deficit to 17-14 with 14:49 to play. Green Bay threatened to add on, but Kaleb Johnson lost a fumble that cornerback Zyon McCollum recovered at the Tampa Bay 4. The Buccaneers were forced to punt, but regained the ball with another takeaway as Jacob Parrish intercepted Love at the Tampa Bay 7 with 4:18 remaining. Tampa Bay advanced as far as the Packers' 46 on its last drive, but Keisean Nixon broke up a fourth-down pass with 1:25 remaining to clinch matters. Daniels was picked off on Tampa Bay's second drive. Evan Williams jumped a route and pulled in the interception at the Packers' 32. Green Bay took advantage as it pieced together a 16-play, 68-yard drive that chewed up more than nine minutes. Love threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden for the game's first score. Tampa Bay evened the score on Sean Tucker's 2-yard rush with 5:13 remaining in the first half. Daniels threw his second interception with less than a minute left before halftime, this time to Edgerrin Cooper. Green Bay finished the half with a 58-yard field goal by Trey Smack for a 10-7 lead at the break. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kyren Williams, Rams run past Eagles
item.description: Kyren Williams rushed for two late touchdowns to rally the Los Angeles Rams to a 24-20 victory against the Eagles on a soggy Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyren Williams rushed for two late touchdowns to rally the Los Angeles Rams to a 24-20 victory against the Eagles on a soggy Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia. Williams scored from 1 yard out with 3:59 left and from 7 yards out with 1:10 remaining to lift the Rams (2-2) over the Eagles (2-2), who had never trailed to that point. Byron Young sealed the win with two sacks on Philadelphia's final drive. Matthew Stafford overcame two first-half interceptions and finished with 317 yards on 32-of-51 passing. Puka Nacua had a touchdown run to go with 125 yards on nine catches and Williams gained 147 yards (80 rushing, 67 receiving) from scrimmage. Jalen Hurts threw two touchdowns to Darius Cooper and Philadelphia built a 20-10 lead by halftime, but the offense largely struggled after losing Saquon Barkley to an early injury and finished 0-for-12 on third-down conversions with only 172 yards of offense. Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 93 yards. Barkley went out with a right hamstring injury on the second snap of the game. The Eagles' short-handed offense was already playing without wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) and right tackle Lane Johnson (personal). The drive on which Barkley got hurt began with the Eagles' first takeaway of the season, an interception by Andrew Mukuba. It ended with Jake Elliott's 29-yard field goal. Philadelphia had been the only NFL team with zero takeaways and zero points in the opening quarter. The Rams made it 3-3 with a 40-yard field goal by Harrison Mevis late in the first quarter. Philadelphia built a 13-3 lead in the second quarter with a 56-yard field goal by Elliott and a juggling, 18-yard catch by Cooper in the end zone. Britain Covey set up Cooper's score with a 41-yard punt return. After missing the previous two games with hip and groin injuries, Nacua scored his third career rushing TD from 2 yards out just after the two-minute warning to pull the Rams within 13-10. Cooper DeJean's 25-yard interception return and a 25-yard pass-interference penalty against Trent McDuffie set up Cooper's second score. Hurts' 10-yard strike with three seconds left gave Philadelphia a 20-10 halftime lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kyle Monangai, Tyson Bagent stand out as Bears flatten Jets
item.description: Kyle Monangai rushed for 146 yards and two touchdowns and Tyson Bagent passed for 268 yards to boost the host Chicago Bears to a 23-12 victory against the New York Jets on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Monangai rushed for 146 yards and two touchdowns and Tyson Bagent passed for 268 yards to boost the host Chicago Bears to a 23-12 victory against the New York Jets on Sunday. Chicago (3-1) limited New York (1-3) to 157 total yards as the Jets lost their third game in a row. The Bears rolled up 492 yards of offense while collecting 34 first downs to the Jets' seven. Bagent finished 25-of-34 passing, Rome Odunze had six catches for 94 yards and Monangai finished with 30 carries. Jason Sanders connected on field goals of 36 and 30 yards for New York, which enjoyed a rare bright spot when safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Bagent in the second quarter. That stopped a record drought of 21 games without an interception for the Jets, who snagged their first pick since Jan. 5, 2025. New York had three potential interceptions nullified by penalty. Bagent started one week after journeyman Case Keenum accounted for three total touchdowns while leading the Bears to a home victory against the Philadelphia Eagles, shining in his first start since December 2023. Bagent was active for the Philadelphia game after spending much of the previous week in concussion protocol. He started sharply against the Jets, completing his first five passes, including gains of 21 and 20 yards to Odunze and Luther Burden III on successive plays. Chicago marched 93 yards on 14 plays on the opening possession but didn't score, as Brandon Stephens stopped D'Andre Swift on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line. The Bears visited the end zone on their next possession, with Monangai converting on fourth-and-goal from the 1 with 23 seconds left in the first quarter. Cairo Santos followed Sanders' first field goal of the afternoon with separate 30-yard field goals over the final 2:29 of the half, giving the Bears a 13-3 edge at intermission. A Sanders field goal pulled the Jets within 13-6 midway through the third quarter before the Bears pulled away with 10 straight points, including a 5-yard Monangai touchdown run to cap a nine-play, 72-yard drive. Geno Smith connected with Isaiah Williams for a 58-yard touchdown pass with 9:16 left, but Sanders missed the point-after attempt. Smith was 8-of-15 passing for 119 yards and a touchdown. Braelon Allen gained 59 yards on 14 carries while Williams had two catches for 73 yards. Jets cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was ruled out with a concussion in the fourth quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jets capitalize on power plays, take down Red Wings
item.description: Kyle Connor scored two power-play goals and added an assist to lift the Winnipeg Jets to a 3-2 victory over the host Detroit Red Wings on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Connor scored two power-play goals and added an assist to lift the Winnipeg Jets to a 3-2 victory over the host Detroit Red Wings on Sunday afternoon. Cole Perfetti scored the other goal and had two assists, while Josh Morrissey added two assists for the Jets, who went 3-for-4 on the power play. Stuart Skinner made 33 saves in Winnipeg's first victory. The Jets lost to Boston in overtime in their season opener Friday. Viktor Arvidsson and Emmitt Finnie scored for the Red Wings and John Gibson stopped 24 shots. Former Detroit captain Dylan Larkin, who has requested a trade, missed the game with an upper-body injury. Forward Marco Kasper was also sidelined by an upper-body injury suffered during the team's 2-0 opening-night loss to the New York Rangers on Friday. Winnipeg goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, a teammate of Larkin's on the gold medal-winning Team USA at the 2026 Winter Olympics, was not with the team after being suspended for failing to show up for training camp. He has also requested a trade. The crowd was riled up with 7:50 left in the opening period, as the Jets' Tyrel Bauer and Wings' Keegan Kolesar dropped the gloves. Along with the fighting penalties, Kolesar was whistled for unsportsmanlike conduct, giving the Jets a power play. They cashed in on Perfetti's goal. Connor passed the puck to Perfetti and the puck was deflected up and over Gibson with 6:56 remaining in the period. At the same time as the goal, Detroit's J.T. Compher was whistled for unsportsmanlike conduct. Once again, Winnipeg converted its power play, as Connor skated to the net and flipped a backhander past Gibson with 5:24 left in the period. Gabriel Vilardi and Perfetti collected the assists. Connor's second power-play goal came after Lucas Raymond was penalized for holding. Connor collected a rebound in the right circle and rifled a shot past Gibson. With Dylan DeMelo in the penalty box for tripping, Arvidsson ended Detroit's drought when he scored in front off an Andrew Copp feed. Moritz Seider had the second assist. Finnie made it 3-2 at 4:56 of the third, converting in front off Michael Brandsegg-Nygard's pass from behind the net. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alaska LNG shipping savings justifies billions in investment, developer says
item.description: Alaska LNG's developer said the project's access to stranded natural gas and shorter shipping routes to Asia will make it competitive with US Gulf Coast rivals, despite questions from some analysts about the project's massive infrastructure costs.
item.dc:creator: Curtis Williams
item.content:encoded: Alaska LNG's developer said the project's access to stranded natural gas and shorter shipping routes to Asia will make it competitive with US Gulf Coast rivals, despite [USN:L1N45N10U TEXT:"questions"] from some analysts about the project's massive infrastructure costs. When the project is completed, the cost of shipping gas to Asia from Alaska's North Slope would be at least 65% cheaper than shipping LNG from the Gulf Coast, Tim Fitzpatrick, communications director for project developer Glenfarne, said on Sunday in an email to Reuters. The proposed project, [USN:S0N43J052 TEXT:"backed"] by President Donald Trump, would move gas from Alaska's North Slope through an 800-mile pipeline to a liquefied natural gas export plant in southern Alaska. A key question has been whether lower shipping costs justify the billions of dollars needed to build the infrastructure. Critics have pointed to the project's estimated cost of $44.5 billion to $54.5 billion, which translates to roughly $2.2 billion to $2.7 billion per million tons per annum (MTPA) of LNG capacity. That appears significantly higher than many recently approved Gulf Coast developments. But developer Glenfarne argues that the comparison is misleading because it includes the expense of pipeline and gas treatment infrastructure needed to bring stranded North Slope gas to market. The Alaska LNG project entails about $1.4 billion per MTPA in delivery costs, Fitzpatrick said. US LNG projects approved since Russia's invasion of Ukraine have generally been built at an average cost of about $1 billion per mtpa or less. Glenfarne argues the project's competitiveness should be measured by delivered LNG costs rather than upfront spending. The company, Fitzpatrick said, so far has identified customers for 13 million tons per year of LNG, and needs 16 million tons annually to support project financing. Trump on Friday said South Korea will help finance the Alaska LNG effort as part of a $200 billion package of investment in US projects. But Seoul quickly suggested that its role in the Alaska project is not yet set.

item.title: Austrian government's No. 2 figure says he will step down
item.description: Austrian Vice Chancellor Andreas Babler said on Sunday he would quit as the second-highest government official and as leader of the ruling Social Democratic Party next year, bowing to growing unrest within the party over its slide in opinion polls.
item.dc:creator: Francois Murphy
item.content:encoded: Austrian Vice Chancellor Andreas Babler said on Sunday he would quit as the second-highest government official and as leader of the ruling Social Democratic Party next year, bowing to growing unrest within the party over its slide in opinion polls. The Social Democrats are the second party in a three-way government led by conservative Chancellor Christian Stocker that was formed last year after the far-right Freedom Party (FPO) won the most seats in a parliamentary election for the first time but was unable to forge a ruling coalition. While the three-party government's formation shut the FPO out of power, the FPO has only gained ground in opinion polls since then. Its support is now running around 38%, more than the Social Democrats and Stocker's People's Party combined. Speculation about Babler's potential departure grew as the Social Democrats' support kept sliding. Recent opinion polls put it on 15%, a fall of about 6 points since the last parliamentary election in September 2024. "Public debates over who the leader should be are not good for political parties. Public disputes are not good for political parties," Babler told a press conference after a day of meetings among senior party figures, adding that the debate over whether he should quit was a distraction. "I am convinced this must end," he said. Finance Minister Markus Marterbauer, who is [USN:L1N43F08U TEXT:"undergoing treatment for cancer"], will replace Babler as vice chancellor early next year and Babler will step down as party leader at the same time, Babler said, adding that he could not say which week the change would happen in.

item.title: France's Schneider Electric nears $20 billion deal to buy US software group PTC, FT reports
item.description: France's Schneider Electric is nearing a deal to buy US software group PTC for about $20 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday citing people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France's Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) is nearing a deal to buy US software group PTC (PTC.O) for about $20 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday citing people with knowledge of the matter. A deal may be announced as soon as Monday, the newspaper said, adding that discussions between the two companies were ongoing and there was no certainty they would result in a deal. Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. Schneider Electric and PTC did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment outside regular business hours. Boston-based PTC has a market value of $15.63 billion, according to LSEG data. In July, the company had lifted its [USN:L4N43V2I2 TEXT:"annual revenue forecast"] after third-quarter results, betting on strong demand for its core industrial software and artificial intelligence-powered tools.

item.title: Report: Seahawks to work out RB Joe Mixon
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks are bringing in free-agent running back Joe Mixon for a workout, Fox Sports reported Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Seahawks are bringing in free-agent running back Joe Mixon for a workout, Fox Sports reported Sunday. The reigning Super Bowl champions are looking to add backfield depth after placing rookie Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve Saturday. Seattle signed Velus Jones Jr. off its practice squad Saturday to take Price's spot on the roster. Zach Charbonnet (knee) will be eligible to return in Week 5. Mixon, 30, played his first seven seasons for the Cincinnati Bengals, eclipsing 1,000 rushing yards in four of them. During that span, he compiled 6,412 yards and 49 touchdowns rushing, to go with 283 receptions for 2,139 yards and 13 receiving touchdowns. In 2024, he joined the Houston Texans, rushing for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns in 14 games. He earned his second career Pro Bowl selection as a result. Mixon missed the 2025 season with a foot injury. The Texans released him last March. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bengals lose WRs Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor)
item.description: Along with losing All-Pro wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion in Sunday's home loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Cincinnati Bengals saw No. 2 receiver Tee Higgins leave the game with an adductor injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Along with losing All-Pro wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion in Sunday's home loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Cincinnati Bengals saw No. 2 receiver Tee Higgins leave the game with an adductor injury. Chase, who had three catches for 27 yards, was ruled out with a concussion after his head hit the turf early in the second quarter of the 22-17 loss. Higgins, who reeled in 11 receptions for 157 yards, exited in the fourth quarter and missed most of the Bengals' last possession that ended at the Jaguars' 12-yard line. In the second quarter, Chase caught a 4-yard pass from Joe Burrow then had his facemask grabbed and pulled by Jaguars cornerback Jarrian Jones. While Chase fell to the ground, linebacker Ventrell Miller dove into Chase and knocked the back of his helmet into the turf. Following a toe-tapping sideline grab late in the game, Higgins injured his adductor. He left briefly and returned for one play on the Bengals' final drive but was unable to continue. Chase, 26, has 21 receptions for 212 yards and three touchdowns over four games this season. In six NFL seasons, all with the Bengals, the five-time Pro Bowl selection has 541 receptions for 7,049 yards and 57 touchdowns. The Bengals selected him with the No. 5 overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft. Higgins, 27, has 25 receptions for 401 yards and one touchdown in four games this season. In his seventh season after Cincinnati selected him in the second round of the 2020 draft, Higgins has 414 catches for 5,842 yards and 46 touchdowns. He earned his first Pro Bowl selection last year, posting a career-high 11 touchdowns. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson (ankle) misses second half, reportedly day-to-day
item.description: Lamar Jackson missed the second half of the Baltimore Ravens' 24-18 win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but NFL Network reported that he's believed to be day-to-day with a left ankle injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson missed the second half of the Baltimore Ravens' 24-18 win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but NFL Network reported that he's believed to be day-to-day with a left ankle injury. Jackson was seen wearing a protective boot as he left the stadium, but Ravens coach Jesse Minter indicated that Jackson avoided a major injury. "He was just dealing with a little bit of an ankle," Minter said postgame. "I don't know enough about it right now, but we'll have to see where that's at." When asked whether Jackson could have returned to the game if Baltimore needed him, Minter said, "There were some talks about that. So, hopefully it's in a good spot." Jackson was initially ruled questionable to return after suffering the injury on his final play of the first half. The two-time MVP quarterback appeared to turn his left ankle when attempting to elude a sack by Jermaine Johnson II, who landed on the ankle as he fell to the ground. Tyler Huntley took over with the Ravens leading 24-7 coming out of halftime. Huntley completed 8 of 9 pass attempts for 63 yards and ran four times for 16 yards, but the Ravens were held scoreless in the half as the Titans made a comeback bid that fell short. Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns and was sacked twice in the first half. He also rushed twice for 20 yards. The Ravens also lost star cornerback Marlon Humphrey (calf), right guard Andrew Vorhees (foot) and tight end Durham Smythe (Achilles) throughout the course of the game. Minter had no additional information about their statuses postgame. --Field Level Media

item.title: Dustin May, Nick Pivetta named Game 3 starters in Brewers-Padres NLDS
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy said Sunday that right-hander Dustin May will start Game 3 of the National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres on Tuesday when the series shifts to San Diego.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy said Sunday that right-hander Dustin May will start Game 3 of the National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres on Tuesday when the series shifts to San Diego. May will square off against right-hander Nick Pivetta, who was named the Padres' Game 3 starter by manager Craig Stammen on Sunday. "He's pitched fantastic against the Padres," Murphy said of May hours before Game 2 of the best-of-five series at American Family Field. "He's got experience and we brought him in to do that." The Brewers won the series opener 3-2 on Saturday. May is 3-5 with a 3.14 ERA in 16 career regular-season games (13 starts) against San Diego. He faced the Padres three times this season, twice with the St. Louis Cardinals and once with the Brewers. He went 1-1 with a 1.23 ERA in those three games, allowing four runs, three earned, in 22 innings. May (7-9, 4.70 ERA), whose postseason roster spot was not a certainty, has been inconsistent with Milwaukee since being acquired at the trade deadline from St. Louis along with reliever JoJo Romero. May was 2-2 with a 5.65 ERA in 10 starts for the Brewers. Home runs were an issue; he gave up seven in 36 2/3 innings after allowing seven in 109 innings for the Cardinals. May lasted more than 3 2/3 innings in just one of his five starts in September. In his last outing, he allowed two runs on three hits, including a homer, in three innings in a 3-2 win over St. Louis. May is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in nine career postseason outings, including three starts, all with the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2019 and 2020. Pivetta (3-2, 2.86 ERA) was 2-0 with a 1.45 ERA in four September starts after missing most of the season with a right elbow injury. He made four starts before going on the IL in mid-April. Pivetta started Game 2 of the Padres' wild-card series against the Chicago Cubs on Wednesday, allowing one run on three hits in 3 1/3 innings. San Diego went on to win 4-1 and complete a two-game sweep of Chicago. Pivetta threw 66 pitches before giving way to the Padres' vaunted bullpen, which Murphy has called the best in baseball. Milwaukee earned a first-round bye and home-field advantage throughout the postseason after winning a franchise-record 103 games. San Diego entered the wild-card round having won 17 of its final 20 games. --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Braves punt on LHP Chris Sale, turn to LHP Ray Kerr in Game 2 of NLDS
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Hoping to have left-hander Chris Sale available to start Game 2 of the National League Division Series on Sunday, the Atlanta Braves turned to left-hander Ray Kerr instead as their starter against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- Hoping to have left-hander Chris Sale available to start Game 2 of the National League Division Series on Sunday, the Atlanta Braves turned to left-hander Ray Kerr instead as their starter against the Los Angeles Dodgers. The Braves had been waiting on Sale's availability after the staff ace recorded the final four outs of the wild-card-round clincher against the Philadelphia Philles on Thursday. "We'll have some conversations about this," Braves manager Walt Weiss said after the Braves' 5-3 road loss in Game 1 of the best-of-five series on Saturday. "So, not sure who's going to start. That's where we're at right now." Sale's next opportunity to start a game will come in Game 3 on Tuesday at Atlanta. The Dodgers already named ace right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto to start that game, creating a matchup of dynamic starters. Sale and Yamamoto squared off Aug. 27, also at Atlanta, and the Braves walked away with a 1-0 victory to finish off a three-game series sweep behind a complete-game shutout from Sale. Kerr, 32, takes the mound after he started Thursday's wild-card clincher against the Phillies when he went 3 1/3 scoreless innings on one hit. Kerr had a 1.47 ERA in nine appearances (one start) for Atlanta during the regular season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Missouri rout of Florida shakes up AP Top 25; top teams unchanged
item.description: Missouri's surprise rout of Florida and Alabama's road blowout of Mississippi State on Saturday generated the most movement in the latest Associated Press Top 25.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Missouri's surprise rout of Florida and Alabama's road blowout of Mississippi State on Saturday generated the most movement in the latest Associated Press Top 25. The Tigers surged from 25th to 14th in the rankings after taking down the Gators 45-17 in Columbia, Mo. Florida tumbled from eighth to 16th one week after reaching the top 10 with a blowout win over Ole Miss. As for the Crimson Tide, they switched places with reigning national champion Indiana, moving into sixth thanks to their 56-23 shellacking of the then-No. 16 Bulldogs in Starkville, Miss. The Hoosiers dropped to seventh despite taking care of Rutgers 47-15. The top five remain unchanged: Texas, which was idle; Georgia, which pulled away in the second half to defeat Vanderbilt 38-14; Notre Dame, which struggled in beating North Carolina 37-26 on the road; Miami (Fla.), which went into Clemson and routed the Tigers 41-13 in prime time; and Ohio State, which toppled then-No. 14 Iowa 31-14 in Iowa City. The Longhorns received 61 of 70 first-place votes from the AP's media panel. Georgia received six first-place votes, Miami got two and Indiana got one. As for the rest of the top 10, BYU moved up from 10th to eighth after beating TCU 17-10 in Fort Worth; Ole Miss, which was idle, remained in ninth, and LSU inched up from 11th to 10th after blowing out FCS McNeese State 63-14. Florida, Mississippi State and Iowa were the only ranked teams to lose in Week 5. Mississippi State dropped to 16th and Iowa fell to 20th. No. 24 Kentucky used a two-point conversion in overtime to edge South Carolina 35-34 in Columbia, S.C., but the Wildcats fell out of the rankings anyway. Pitt, at 25th, took their place. The Panthers edged Virginia Tech 35-33 on Friday in a game marked by controversy. The ACC officials posted under the goal posts ruled a game-winning field-goal attempt by the Hokies no good as time expired. Replays made the call appear less clear. AP Top 25 1. Texas 2. Georgia 3. item.title: Vídeo não mostra helicópteros dos EUA no Brasil durante eleições
item.description: Um vídeo de supostos helicópteros dos Estados Unidos não tem relação com as eleições brasileiras que ocorrem neste domingo, ao contrário do que afirmam posts no Instagram. O registro está disponível na plataforma há mais de um mês e tem um rótulo indicando que as imagens foram criadas por IA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo de supostos helicópteros dos Estados Unidos não tem relação com as eleições brasileiras que ocorrem neste domingo, ao contrário do que afirmam posts no Instagram. O registro está disponível na plataforma há mais de um mês e tem um rótulo indicando que as imagens foram criadas por IA. Estes são os principais detalhes: As imagens parecem ter sido feitas a partir de um veículo em movimento, enquanto helicópteros militares sobrevoam uma área descampada. “Estamos chegando, Brasil”, narra um homem ao fundo. A mesma gravação circula no Instagram ao menos desde 19 de agosto de 2026, quando foi compartilhada com o aviso “Conteúdo de IA” e a localização “Estados Unidos da América”. “Eu ‘tava’ na estrada por aqui quando comecei a ver essa movimentação e pensei: ‘Rapaz… o Brasil vai receber visita!’”, diz a legenda da postagem , publicada no perfil de um brasileiro que diz morar nos EUA. O autor do post respondeu a um comentário que apontou o uso de IA que “você não sabe brincar, não, olha a legenda”. Até o momento, não há registros de que o governo dos EUA tenha enviado helicópteros ao Brasil em meio às eleições. Uma possível interferência dos EUA no pleito preocupa autoridades brasileiras e é alvo de uma investigação da Polícia Federal (PF). Veredicto: falso. O vídeo de supostos helicópteros dos EUA no Brasil nas vésperas das eleições circula desde agosto com um rótulo de IA. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: AkzoNobel to sell Southeast Asia paints business to Nippon Paint for $1.35 billion
item.description: AkzoNobel said on Monday it has agreed to sell its Southeast Asian decorative paints business to Nippon Paint for $1.35 billion, completing a review of its Asian decorative paints portfolio.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: AkzoNobel (AKZO.AS) said on Monday it has agreed to sell its Southeast Asian decorative paints business to Nippon Paint (4612.T) for $1.35 billion, completing a review of its Asian decorative paints portfolio. The sale covers decorative paints operations in Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Papua New Guinea and Australia, the Dutch paints maker said, adding that it expects net cash proceeds of about $1 billion after tax and payments to minority partners. The Dulux paintmaker earlier divested its decorative paints operations in [USN:L4N3SU06N TEXT:"India "]and [USN:FWN40Z1CF TEXT:"Pakistan "]for $1.6 billion and 50 million euros, respectively. "The successful completion of our Asia portfolio review is part of an ongoing strategy to focus our portfolio on areas where we can achieve differentiating scale and strengthen our position," AkzoNobel Chief Executive Greg Poux-Guillaume said in a statement. The Indonesia deal is expected to close separately in late 2026, while the remaining transactions are expected to close around mid-2027. AkzoNobel said it will now focus on the successful closing of its merger with US coatings maker [USN:L8N3WU04N TEXT:"Axalta "] (AXTA.N) , which was announced in November last year. Nippon Paint submitted [USN:L6N43F003 TEXT:"multiple proposals"] to acquire AkzoNobel's decorative paints business, the Dutch company said in July, valuing it at about €7.5 billion ($8.44 billion). That approach followed the [USN:L6N42B0EM TEXT:"withdrawal"] of a €12.5 billion bid for the entire company that Nippon Paint had pursued jointly with US-based paintmaker Sherwin-Williams (SHW.N) in June. The Financial Times, which earlier reported the Southeast Asia deal, said Nippon remains interested in a larger deal for the decorative paint business, but that integration of the Southeast Asia business could occupy the company for some time and AkzoNobel does not have plans to sell further assets from the business. ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: Manchester City beat hapless Arsenal 4-2 to stay top of WSL
item.description: Lauren Hemp scored twice as Manchester City came from behind on two occasions to beat Arsenal 4-2 in the Women's Super League on Sunday, keeping the champions top of the table heading into the international break after a fifth straight win from their opening five matches.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lauren Hemp scored twice as Manchester City came from behind on two occasions to beat Arsenal 4-2 in the Women's Super League on Sunday, keeping the champions top of the table heading into the international break after a fifth straight win from their opening five matches. Arsenal went ahead through Lisa Baum in the 43rd minute, but City levelled when Hemp forced the ball home from a tight angle in first-half stoppage time. Alessia Russo put the Gunners back in front four minutes after the break but again City came back, Kerstin Casparij equalising in the 63rd minute before Hemp put them in front for the first time nine minutes later. Striker Bunny Shaw sealed the three points in the 84th minute with her fifth goal of the season to condemn Arsenal, who are without a win since the opening day of the season, to their second straight defeat after losing 1-0 away to Chelsea last week. The loss leaves Arsenal in 10th spot on five points from five games after a dismal start to the campaign. Earlier in the afternoon, Sonia Bompastor's Chelsea thumped West Ham United 3-0 to put them into second place, two points behind City. They took the lead thanks to a Melvine Malard strike and added two late goals through Keira Walsh and Maika Hamano. London City Lionesses showed that they will be a force to be reckoned with in the title race, Alexia Putellas scoring twice in the first half of a 6-1 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur, who were left shell-shocked by the pressing of the visitors. Spurs had only conceded two goals in the first four outings, but they were hit for six as London City notched their third successive win in impressive fashion to move to third place on 12 points. Charlton Athletic, who are still searching for their first point since being promoted, remain bottom of the 14-team table after a 5-1 hammering at the hands of Brighton & Hove Albion, with Kiko Seike scoring twice for the Seagulls. Everton's strong start to the season continued with a 2-1 win over Birmingham City that lifts them to fifth spot in the table on nine points, two ahead of cross-town rivals Liverpool, who lost 1-0 to Manchester United on Saturday.

item.title: South Africa's Nortje eyes test return against Australia after lengthy absence
item.description: South Africa fast bowler Anrich Nortje could make a remarkable return to first-class cricket after an absence of almost four years to help an injury-hampered South Africa attack in the first test against Australia, which starts in Durban on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa fast bowler Anrich Nortje could make a remarkable return to first-class cricket after an absence of almost four years to help an injury-hampered South Africa attack in the first test against Australia, which starts in Durban on Friday. With fitness doubts over pace spearhead Kagiso Rabada and three other bowlers ruled out with hamstring injuries, Nortje is set to return to red-ball cricket for the first time since South Africa's test victory over West Indies in March 2023. That match, in which he took 5-36 in the first innings, was Nortje's last first-class appearance. A succession of injury setbacks, as he struggled with back and hip problems, subsequently led him to focus on the shorter formats, where bowling in brief spells has helped reduce the strain on his body. The 32-year-old has evolved into a T20 specialist, but said on Sunday he had been working on his red-ball skills. "It's been quite a bit of a focus for me to try and execute skills with the red ball, to build loads gradually and in the right way try and get the overs up,” he told reporters on Sunday. “It's something that I've been doing for quite some time. There's been quite some effort put in to try and upskill again, and improve from where I left off. "I'll be very excited if I can put my test cap on again. Growing up, it's the format you want to play. It's the motivation when you train," he added. Nortje has featured in 19 tests with a bowling average of 26.71 and regularly bowled at speeds in excess of 145kph – with his action taking a heavy toll on his body. TEST CRICKET BRINGS OUT EXTRA FIRE "You don't think of the tough times in T20 cricket. You just think about executing skills there, whereas in tests, you think about the tough times, the good times, the hard work and think that gets you through some sessions. "There's just that little bit of extra X-factor that comes out, or fire that comes out, and energy that comes out," Nortje added. "Guys want to do well, and everyone wants to perform. It is a big series." South Africa started an intra-squad match on Sunday and late Monday will cut their preliminary squad from 18 to 15, with Nortje expected to make the cut despite his lengthy absence. "The guys have grown quite a bit,” he said of the test side which has since gone on to win the World Test Championship, beating Australia in mid-2025. “They've played a lot and they've done really well. Hopefully, I can just add on to that. I'm very keen to get going and be on the park and try to do well for the country," Nortje added.

item.title: Valkyries' Janelle Salaun unanimous choice as Sixth Player of Year
item.description: Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaun was unanimously selected as the 2026 WNBA Sixth Player of the Year, the league announced Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaun was unanimously selected as the 2026 WNBA Sixth Player of the Year, the league announced Sunday. Salaun earned the honor for the first time after receiving all 74 votes from a national panel of sportswriters and broadcasters. A player had to play more games as a reserve than as a starter to be eligible for the award. Salaun, 25, led all WNBA reserves in scoring with 12.7 points per game. The 6-foot-2 France native came off the bench in all 40 of the games in which she played, setting league single-season records for points (509) and 3-pointers made (93) by a reserve. Naz Hillmon of the Atlanta Dream won the award last year. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) seen walking normally after loss to Rams
